content.value_statement: Prisma Client tasks can require many query options, relation patterns, and transaction choices. This reference helps you select documented APIs and use raw SQL more safely.
actual_capabilities: Explains Prisma Client construction with adapters and configuration options.
Guides CRUD queries, bulk operations, selections, relations, and pagination.
Lists scalar, logical, and relation filter patterns.
Provides transaction patterns for related database operations.
Explains client lifecycle methods, events, and extensions.
Shows parameterized raw SQL patterns and warns about unsafe query construction.
limitations: It is a reference skill and does not inspect your Prisma schema or database.
Examples require adaptation to your models, provider, and Prisma version.
It does not run migrations, execute queries, or validate production permissions.
Raw SQL remains your responsibility to review, parameterize, and authorize.

use_cases.title: Create application queries
use_cases.description: Use documented CRUD, filters, and query shapes while implementing a TypeScript service.

use_cases.title: Review database access
use_cases.description: Check selections, relation loading, pagination, and transaction choices during code review.

use_cases.title: Learn raw SQL safeguards
use_cases.description: Compare parameterized Prisma SQL patterns with unsafe concatenation before adding database-specific queries.

prompt_templates.title: Find a user by email
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a Prisma Client query to find one user by email and select only id, email, and name.

prompt_templates.title: Filter and paginate records
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write a Prisma findMany query for active users, sorted by creation date, with cursor pagination.

prompt_templates.title: Create related records safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to create a user and an initial post in one Prisma operation. Explain the relation fields I must adapt.

prompt_templates.title: Review a raw SQL plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned Prisma raw SQL query. Identify parameterization requirements and suggest a safer tagged-template approach.

output_examples.input: I need recent published posts with each author name.
output: A findMany query pattern using a published filter and descending creation-date order.
An include or select recommendation that returns only the needed author fields.
A reminder to limit result size and index the filter and sort columns.

output_examples.input: Can I build a raw SQL query from a user-selected table name?
output: A warning that identifiers cannot be parameterized like values.
Guidance to use a fixed allowlist for supported identifiers.
A parameterized pattern for all user-provided values.

best_practices: Select only the fields and relations required by the caller.
Use transactions for related writes that must succeed or fail together.
Use tagged templates and parameters for raw SQL values.
anti_patterns: Do not concatenate user input into raw SQL strings.
Do not expose database URLs or query parameters in application logs.
Do not use broad relation includes when a focused select is sufficient.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Prisma Client setup, queries, filters, relations, transactions, methods, and raw SQL safety.

faq.question: Does it execute database commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference guidance and examples only.

faq.question: Can it generate queries for my models?
faq.answer: Yes, it can suggest patterns, but you must adapt model and field names to your schema.

faq.question: When should I use raw SQL?
faq.answer: Use it only when Prisma query APIs are insufficient and prefer parameterized tagged templates.

faq.question: Does it protect against SQL injection automatically?
faq.answer: No. You must parameterize values and avoid untrusted dynamic identifiers and string concatenation.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The package declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
